chunk_findings.detail: `_eta` computes `running_left_s` from only slots where `_held` is true, so it ignores idle slots. If `slots_n` is larger than the number of held slots, the earliest available slot is immediately free, but `_eta` still passes the minimum remaining time of the held slots. For example, with `slots_n=2`, slot 0 held with note `{"cost_s": 600, "at": now}`, slot 1 free, and waiting line `[a, b]`, `_eta` passes `running_left_s=600` for `b`; `SQ.estimate` therefore adds a 10-minute offset even though slot 1 is idle and `a` can start now. The ETA is wrong (overestimated) whenever at least one slot is free while another held slot has a positive estimate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_eta

chunk_findings.detail: The `contextlib.suppress(OSError, ValueError, TypeError)` around the held-slot note read does not cover a missing `at` key. Given a slot note file containing `{"cost_s": 100}` (or `{}`), `_held` can be true, `json.loads` succeeds, `held.get("cost_s")` succeeds, then `float(held["at"])` raises `KeyError`, which is not suppressed and propagates. This crashes the queue-status/Blocked path instead of treating the note as unreadable, even though the code explicitly tries to tolerate malformed slot notes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_eta

chunk_findings.detail: A held slot whose note lacks `cost_s` is treated as having zero seconds left. Given a held slot note `{"at": now-1}` with no `cost_s`, `held.get("cost_s") or 0.0` yields `0.0`, so `left` receives `0` and `running_left_s` becomes `0`. The estimate then says a running suite will free a slot immediately even though it may run for hours. Missing predicted cost should fall back to a default or be skipped, not be interpreted as “about to finish now.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_eta

chunk_findings.detail: When `_note_of` returns `None`—a case the new code explicitly handles with `(mine or ("", 0.0))[1]` and `if mine is not None:`—the slot note is written with `cost_s: 0.0`. The code then still calls `_eta(line, name, slots_n, directory)` to build the `SuiteBusy` estimate. Thus a holder whose class/scope cannot be estimated is advertised as having zero remaining work. For example, if no `[suites].class_patterns` match holder `agent:foo` (or the cost lookup yields `None`), it can hold a suite slot for 30 minutes, but a waiter behind it sees the holder note with `cost_s=0.0` and the ETA calculation treats that slot as already free, so the busy line reports an estimated wait of 0m or otherwise far too low. The `default_cost_s` knob exists for missing estimates, but this path bypasses it and uses zero.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:suite_lock

chunk_findings.detail: The fair-share stage can let one agent take all offered slots. Example: `slots=2`, `agent_share=0.2`, and six waiting tickets: five short `item` tickets from agent `A` (`cost_s=1`) plus one long `item` ticket from agent `B` (`cost_s=100000`). `cap=max(1, math.ceil(0.2*6))=2`; the short A tickets sort first, so `kept` receives A1, A2, B and the remaining A tickets are deferred, yielding an order beginning `A1, A2, B, ...`. Filling two slots from that order gives both slots to A. With one slot and a continuous supply of short A tickets, B is kept behind the current A ticket after each recomputation and can be delayed arbitrarily by choosing a large `max_wait_factor`/`cost_s`, so the “fair share” cap on the current waiting list does not actually bound slot allocation or prevent starvation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitequeue.py:order

chunk_findings.detail: The aging bound is not honored once fair share is applied. Example: `max_wait_factor=1`, `agent_share=0.2`, `default_cost_s=10`, and waiting tickets `A1` (`cost_s=10`, `waited_s=100`) and `A2` (`cost_s=10`, `waited_s=10`) from agent `A`, plus `B1`, `C1`, `D1` (`cost_s=1000`, `waited_s=0`) from different agents. Both A tickets are overdue (`10 >= 1*10`), but `cap=1`, so the returned order is `A1, B1, C1, D1, A2`. With `slots=2`, the second slot goes to non-overdue `B1` while overdue `A2` waits, directly contradicting the module contract that an overdue ticket “goes first” and “nothing waits past that bound whatever arrives behind it.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitequeue.py:order

chunk_findings.detail: `estimate` uses raw `Waiting.cost_s` for both the wait and the predicted run, but the module contract says a cost of `0` means unknown and counts as `default_cost_s`. Because `estimate` has no `default_cost_s` parameter, an ordered queue in which every ticket has `cost_s=0.0` (unknown measured cost) returns `wait_s=0.0` and `predicted_s=0.0` for the last ticket when `slots=1` and `running_left_s=0.0`, even though each unknown ticket should contribute the configured default (for example, 60 seconds). This underestimates the ETA for queues of tickets whose cost has not yet been measured.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitequeue.py:estimate

chunk_findings.detail: Given `waiting = [W("a", cost=600), W("b", cost=300), W("me", cost=60)]`, `slots=2`, and `running_left_s=0.0`, line 84 asserts `two["wait_s"] == 450.0`. With two free slots, the two tickets ahead of `me` can both start immediately; `me` can start as soon as the shorter of the two ahead tickets finishes, i.e. after 300 seconds. The asserted 450 seconds is therefore a 150-second overestimate and encodes an estimate that can idle an available slot from 300s to 450s.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_queue_priority.py:84

chunk_findings.detail: When a ticket note has no `agent`, `_ordered` uses the full ticket filename as the agent identity: `str(note.get("agent") or n)`. Ticket filenames are created in `_Ticket.__init__` as `f"{time.time_ns():020d}-{key}.ticket"`, where `key` is the stable holder key. Thus two tickets from the same holder differ by timestamp and become distinct “agents” if their notes are missing (for example, tickets already queued before `[suites]` was enabled, or tickets whose note write failed). With `agent_share` enabled, `SQ.order` cannot group those tickets under one holder, so a single holder’s backlog can bypass the per-agent fair-share limit and occupy all slots, starving other agents. The fallback should use the stable key part of the filename or a shared unknown-agent bucket, not the full filename.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_ordered

chunk_findings.detail: `order` applies the agent fair-share filter after aging, and deferred tickets are appended after every kept ticket. This can put an OVERDUE ticket behind a non-overdue ticket from another agent, violating the documented aging bound (“nothing waits past that bound whatever arrives behind it”). Example: with `max_wait_factor=1.0`, `agent_share=0.5`, `default_cost_s=1.0`, and waiting tickets `[Waiting('a1','item',1,'A',10), Waiting('a2','item',1,'A',10), Waiting('a3','item',1,'A',10), Waiting('b','item',1,'B',0)]`, all three `a*` tickets are overdue (`waited_s >= 1 * max(1, 1)`). They rank ahead of `b`, but `cap = ceil(0.5 * 4) = 2`, so `a3` is deferred and the returned order is `a1, a2, b, a3`. With one available slot, `b` runs before `a3` even though `a3` has already exceeded its aging bound.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitequeue.py:86

chunk_findings.detail: `estimate` uses the raw `Waiting.cost_s` value, while `order` treats `cost_s <= 0` as unknown and substitutes `default_cost_s`. Therefore an unknown-cost ticket produces a zero ETA. Example: with `default_cost_s=3600.0`, `ordered = [Waiting('a','item',0.0,'A',0.0), Waiting('b','item',0.0,'B',0.0)]`, `estimate(ordered, 'b', slots=1, running_left_s=0.0)` returns `wait_s=0.0` and `predicted_s=0.0`, but the ordering treats both tickets as 3600-second runs, so the displayed “estimated wait” and “predicted” values are wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitequeue.py:96

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts that `SQ.estimate` puts `me` at position 3 behind `a` and `b`, but the waiting list is not in the queue order the change itself defines. All three tickets are default `item` class and default agent, and their costs are 600, 300, and 60; by `test_within_a_class_the_shortest_predicted_run_goes_first`, the ordered queue is `["me", "b", "a"]`. If `SQ.estimate` honors the queue order, the expected values are wrong (`me` should be position 1 with wait 0). If `SQ.estimate` ignores the ordering and the test passes, the test validates an estimate that can tell a short ticket it is behind two longer tickets even though the queue would run it first.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_queue_priority.py:test_the_estimate_counts_the_cost_ahead_over_the_slots

chunk_findings.detail: The final assertion uses `set(got) == {...}` and only checks `got[0]`, so it can pass on a wrong execution history. For example, if a waiter body runs twice because of a retry or double-release, `got` could be `["fix-Bmain-red-boom", "item-1", "item-1", "item-2"]`; the set equality still succeeds and the first item is still the fix, even though `item-1` ran twice. The same assertion also passes if `item-2` overtakes the older `item-1`, so it does not actually verify the intended order through the lock.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_queue_priority.py:test_a_queued_fix_of_red_main_overtakes_older_item_runs_through_the_lock

chunk_findings.detail: The fix for the previously-confirmed "costless holder note is advertised as zero remaining work" only holds while the holder has been running *less* than `cfg_default`. For a held slot whose note has no `cost_s` — which is now the *normal* note for any holder where `mine is None` (the writer deliberately omits the key, per the new comment "without a predicted cost the note says none") — `_eta` seeds `left = float(cfg_default)` and then unconditionally subtracts elapsed time, so once `now - held["at"] >= cfg_default` the clamp gives `left = 0.0` and the comment's promise ("the default, never 'about to finish'") is false. Concretely: `slots_n=1`, the only slot held with note `{"holder": "agent:foo", "at": now - 7200}` (no `cost_s`), waiting line `[me]`; `busy=[0.0]`, `free=[0.0]`, so `SQ.estimate` sees a slot free *now* and the gate status prints an estimated wait of ~0m for a suite that has already held the slot for two hours. With `slots_n=2` and both slots held by such unknown-cost runs, `free=[0.0, 0.0]` and every queued ticket is told it can start immediately. The probe test `test_a_malformed_or_costless_holder_note_does_not_break_the_estimate` passes as long as the note's `at` is recent, so it does not cover this residual case; an unknown-cost holder should contribute a positive remaining estimate (e.g. the default, or default plus elapsed), not zero, since the slot is provably still held.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `overdue` bypass in the fair-share stage is not counted against the agent’s cap, so an agent can lead its overdue tickets *plus* `cap` non-overdue tickets. For example, with `slots=2`, `agent_share=0.2`, `max_wait_factor=1`, and `default_cost_s=10`, let the waiting tickets be `a1` (agent `A`, cost `10`, waited `10`, overdue), `a2` (agent `A`, cost `1`, waited `0`), and `b`, `c` from agents `B` and `C` (cost `1`, waited `0`). The cap is `max(1, ceil(0.2*4)) = 1`. Ranking puts `a1` first as overdue; the loop keeps `a1` without incrementing `seen[A]`, then keeps `a2` as `seen[A]=1`, then keeps `b`. The returned order begins `a1, a2, b, c`, so filling two slots gives both slots to agent `A`, violating the fair-share acceptance that one agent cannot take all slots.

chunk_findings.detail: The new “do not break the estimate” handling for malformed slot notes is incomplete: it suppresses `OSError`, `ValueError`, `TypeError`, and `KeyError`, but not `AttributeError`. If a slot note contains valid JSON that is not a mapping — for example `[]`, `null`, or `"x"` — `json.loads()` succeeds and the next line `held.get("cost_s")` raises `AttributeError`, which escapes `_eta` and crashes the queue wait/status path. This is exactly the kind of “malformed holder note” the change claims to tolerate; a note file containing `[]` is a concrete input that makes the estimate path fail.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `if overdue(w): kept.append(w); continue` makes overdue tickets bypass the fair-share counter entirely, so an agent's overdue tickets do not consume its `agent_share` allowance for subsequent non-overdue tickets. For example, with `agent_share=0.25` and the usual cap `max(1, int(len(waiting) * agent_share))`, four waiting tickets give `cap=1`. Suppose `max_wait_factor=20` and the ranked queue is `[Waiting('a-old','item',1,'A',100), Waiting('a-new','item',1,'A',10), Waiting('b1','item',1,'B',9), Waiting('b2','item',1,'B',9)]`. `a-old` is overdue and is kept without incrementing `seen['A']`; then `a-new` is kept because `seen['A']` becomes 1 <= cap, while `b2` is deferred. Agent A therefore has two tickets in the kept queue although the fair-share cap is one and only four tickets are waiting, and with one slot it receives the first two runs. This violates the documented per-agent fair share; overdue tickets should still be counted against the agent's share even though they are not deferred.

chunk_findings.detail: `_eta` computes `running_left_s` from only slots where `_held` is true, so it ignores idle slots. If `slots_n` is larger than the number of held slots, the earliest available slot is immediately free, but `_eta` still passes the minimum remaining time of the held slots. For example, with `slots_n=2`, slot 0 held with note `{"cost_s": 600, "at": now}`, slot 1 free, and waiting line `[a, b]`, `_eta` passes `running_left_s=600` for `b`; `SQ.estimate` therefore adds a 10-minute offset even though slot 1 is idle and `a` can start now. The ETA is wrong (overestimated) whenever at least one slot is free while another held slot has a positive estimate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_eta

chunk_findings.detail: The `contextlib.suppress(OSError, ValueError, TypeError)` around the held-slot note read does not cover a missing `at` key. Given a slot note file containing `{"cost_s": 100}` (or `{}`), `_held` can be true, `json.loads` succeeds, `held.get("cost_s")` succeeds, then `float(held["at"])` raises `KeyError`, which is not suppressed and propagates. This crashes the queue-status/Blocked path instead of treating the note as unreadable, even though the code explicitly tries to tolerate malformed slot notes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_eta

chunk_findings.detail: A held slot whose note lacks `cost_s` is treated as having zero seconds left. Given a held slot note `{"at": now-1}` with no `cost_s`, `held.get("cost_s") or 0.0` yields `0.0`, so `left` receives `0` and `running_left_s` becomes `0`. The estimate then says a running suite will free a slot immediately even though it may run for hours. Missing predicted cost should fall back to a default or be skipped, not be interpreted as “about to finish now.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_eta

chunk_findings.detail: When `_note_of` returns `None`—a case the new code explicitly handles with `(mine or ("", 0.0))[1]` and `if mine is not None:`—the slot note is written with `cost_s: 0.0`. The code then still calls `_eta(line, name, slots_n, directory)` to build the `SuiteBusy` estimate. Thus a holder whose class/scope cannot be estimated is advertised as having zero remaining work. For example, if no `[suites].class_patterns` match holder `agent:foo` (or the cost lookup yields `None`), it can hold a suite slot for 30 minutes, but a waiter behind it sees the holder note with `cost_s=0.0` and the ETA calculation treats that slot as already free, so the busy line reports an estimated wait of 0m or otherwise far too low. The `default_cost_s` knob exists for missing estimates, but this path bypasses it and uses zero.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:suite_lock

chunk_findings.detail: The fair-share stage can let one agent take all offered slots. Example: `slots=2`, `agent_share=0.2`, and six waiting tickets: five short `item` tickets from agent `A` (`cost_s=1`) plus one long `item` ticket from agent `B` (`cost_s=100000`). `cap=max(1, math.ceil(0.2*6))=2`; the short A tickets sort first, so `kept` receives A1, A2, B and the remaining A tickets are deferred, yielding an order beginning `A1, A2, B, ...`. Filling two slots from that order gives both slots to A. With one slot and a continuous supply of short A tickets, B is kept behind the current A ticket after each recomputation and can be delayed arbitrarily by choosing a large `max_wait_factor`/`cost_s`, so the “fair share” cap on the current waiting list does not actually bound slot allocation or prevent starvation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitequeue.py:order

chunk_findings.detail: The aging bound is not honored once fair share is applied. Example: `max_wait_factor=1`, `agent_share=0.2`, `default_cost_s=10`, and waiting tickets `A1` (`cost_s=10`, `waited_s=100`) and `A2` (`cost_s=10`, `waited_s=10`) from agent `A`, plus `B1`, `C1`, `D1` (`cost_s=1000`, `waited_s=0`) from different agents. Both A tickets are overdue (`10 >= 1*10`), but `cap=1`, so the returned order is `A1, B1, C1, D1, A2`. With `slots=2`, the second slot goes to non-overdue `B1` while overdue `A2` waits, directly contradicting the module contract that an overdue ticket “goes first” and “nothing waits past that bound whatever arrives behind it.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitequeue.py:order

chunk_findings.detail: `estimate` uses raw `Waiting.cost_s` for both the wait and the predicted run, but the module contract says a cost of `0` means unknown and counts as `default_cost_s`. Because `estimate` has no `default_cost_s` parameter, an ordered queue in which every ticket has `cost_s=0.0` (unknown measured cost) returns `wait_s=0.0` and `predicted_s=0.0` for the last ticket when `slots=1` and `running_left_s=0.0`, even though each unknown ticket should contribute the configured default (for example, 60 seconds). This underestimates the ETA for queues of tickets whose cost has not yet been measured.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitequeue.py:estimate

chunk_findings.detail: Given `waiting = [W("a", cost=600), W("b", cost=300), W("me", cost=60)]`, `slots=2`, and `running_left_s=0.0`, line 84 asserts `two["wait_s"] == 450.0`. With two free slots, the two tickets ahead of `me` can both start immediately; `me` can start as soon as the shorter of the two ahead tickets finishes, i.e. after 300 seconds. The asserted 450 seconds is therefore a 150-second overestimate and encodes an estimate that can idle an available slot from 300s to 450s.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_queue_priority.py:84

chunk_findings.detail: The fix for the previously-confirmed "costless holder note is advertised as zero remaining work" only holds while the holder has been running *less* than `cfg_default`. For a held slot whose note has no `cost_s` — which is now the *normal* note for any holder where `mine is None` (the writer deliberately omits the key, per the new comment "without a predicted cost the note says none") — `_eta` seeds `left = float(cfg_default)` and then unconditionally subtracts elapsed time, so once `now - held["at"] >= cfg_default` the clamp gives `left = 0.0` and the comment's promise ("the default, never 'about to finish'") is false. Concretely: `slots_n=1`, the only slot held with note `{"holder": "agent:foo", "at": now - 7200}` (no `cost_s`), waiting line `[me]`; `busy=[0.0]`, `free=[0.0]`, so `SQ.estimate` sees a slot free *now* and the gate status prints an estimated wait of ~0m for a suite that has already held the slot for two hours. With `slots_n=2` and both slots held by such unknown-cost runs, `free=[0.0, 0.0]` and every queued ticket is told it can start immediately. The probe test `test_a_malformed_or_costless_holder_note_does_not_break_the_estimate` passes as long as the note's `at` is recent, so it does not cover this residual case; an unknown-cost holder should contribute a positive remaining estimate (e.g. the default, or default plus elapsed), not zero, since the slot is provably still held.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_eta (line `left = max(0.0, left - (now - float(held["at"])))`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new `overdue` bypass in the fair-share stage is not counted against the agent’s cap, so an agent can lead its overdue tickets *plus* `cap` non-overdue tickets. For example, with `slots=2`, `agent_share=0.2`, `max_wait_factor=1`, and `default_cost_s=10`, let the waiting tickets be `a1` (agent `A`, cost `10`, waited `10`, overdue), `a2` (agent `A`, cost `1`, waited `0`), and `b`, `c` from agents `B` and `C` (cost `1`, waited `0`). The cap is `max(1, ceil(0.2*4)) = 1`. Ranking puts `a1` first as overdue; the loop keeps `a1` without incrementing `seen[A]`, then keeps `a2` as `seen[A]=1`, then keeps `b`. The returned order begins `a1, a2, b, c`, so filling two slots gives both slots to agent `A`, violating the fair-share acceptance that one agent cannot take all slots.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitequeue.py:87

chunk_findings.detail: When a ticket note has no `agent`, `_ordered` uses the full ticket filename as the agent identity: `str(note.get("agent") or n)`. Ticket filenames are created in `_Ticket.__init__` as `f"{time.time_ns():020d}-{key}.ticket"`, where `key` is the stable holder key. Thus two tickets from the same holder differ by timestamp and become distinct “agents” if their notes are missing (for example, tickets already queued before `[suites]` was enabled, or tickets whose note write failed). With `agent_share` enabled, `SQ.order` cannot group those tickets under one holder, so a single holder’s backlog can bypass the per-agent fair-share limit and occupy all slots, starving other agents. The fallback should use the stable key part of the filename or a shared unknown-agent bucket, not the full filename.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_ordered

chunk_findings.detail: `order` applies the agent fair-share filter after aging, and deferred tickets are appended after every kept ticket. This can put an OVERDUE ticket behind a non-overdue ticket from another agent, violating the documented aging bound (“nothing waits past that bound whatever arrives behind it”). Example: with `max_wait_factor=1.0`, `agent_share=0.5`, `default_cost_s=1.0`, and waiting tickets `[Waiting('a1','item',1,'A',10), Waiting('a2','item',1,'A',10), Waiting('a3','item',1,'A',10), Waiting('b','item',1,'B',0)]`, all three `a*` tickets are overdue (`waited_s >= 1 * max(1, 1)`). They rank ahead of `b`, but `cap = ceil(0.5 * 4) = 2`, so `a3` is deferred and the returned order is `a1, a2, b, a3`. With one available slot, `b` runs before `a3` even though `a3` has already exceeded its aging bound.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitequeue.py:86

chunk_findings.detail: `estimate` uses the raw `Waiting.cost_s` value, while `order` treats `cost_s <= 0` as unknown and substitutes `default_cost_s`. Therefore an unknown-cost ticket produces a zero ETA. Example: with `default_cost_s=3600.0`, `ordered = [Waiting('a','item',0.0,'A',0.0), Waiting('b','item',0.0,'B',0.0)]`, `estimate(ordered, 'b', slots=1, running_left_s=0.0)` returns `wait_s=0.0` and `predicted_s=0.0`, but the ordering treats both tickets as 3600-second runs, so the displayed “estimated wait” and “predicted” values are wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitequeue.py:96

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts that `SQ.estimate` puts `me` at position 3 behind `a` and `b`, but the waiting list is not in the queue order the change itself defines. All three tickets are default `item` class and default agent, and their costs are 600, 300, and 60; by `test_within_a_class_the_shortest_predicted_run_goes_first`, the ordered queue is `["me", "b", "a"]`. If `SQ.estimate` honors the queue order, the expected values are wrong (`me` should be position 1 with wait 0). If `SQ.estimate` ignores the ordering and the test passes, the test validates an estimate that can tell a short ticket it is behind two longer tickets even though the queue would run it first.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_queue_priority.py:test_the_estimate_counts_the_cost_ahead_over_the_slots

chunk_findings.detail: The final assertion uses `set(got) == {...}` and only checks `got[0]`, so it can pass on a wrong execution history. For example, if a waiter body runs twice because of a retry or double-release, `got` could be `["fix-Bmain-red-boom", "item-1", "item-1", "item-2"]`; the set equality still succeeds and the first item is still the fix, even though `item-1` ran twice. The same assertion also passes if `item-2` overtakes the older `item-1`, so it does not actually verify the intended order through the lock.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_queue_priority.py:test_a_queued_fix_of_red_main_overtakes_older_item_runs_through_the_lock

chunk_findings.detail: The new “do not break the estimate” handling for malformed slot notes is incomplete: it suppresses `OSError`, `ValueError`, `TypeError`, and `KeyError`, but not `AttributeError`. If a slot note contains valid JSON that is not a mapping — for example `[]`, `null`, or `"x"` — `json.loads()` succeeds and the next line `held.get("cost_s")` raises `AttributeError`, which escapes `_eta` and crashes the queue wait/status path. This is exactly the kind of “malformed holder note” the change claims to tolerate; a note file containing `[]` is a concrete input that makes the estimate path fail.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_eta

chunk_findings.detail: The new `if overdue(w): kept.append(w); continue` makes overdue tickets bypass the fair-share counter entirely, so an agent's overdue tickets do not consume its `agent_share` allowance for subsequent non-overdue tickets. For example, with `agent_share=0.25` and the usual cap `max(1, int(len(waiting) * agent_share))`, four waiting tickets give `cap=1`. Suppose `max_wait_factor=20` and the ranked queue is `[Waiting('a-old','item',1,'A',100), Waiting('a-new','item',1,'A',10), Waiting('b1','item',1,'B',9), Waiting('b2','item',1,'B',9)]`. `a-old` is overdue and is kept without incrementing `seen['A']`; then `a-new` is kept because `seen['A']` becomes 1 <= cap, while `b2` is deferred. Agent A therefore has two tickets in the kept queue although the fair-share cap is one and only four tickets are waiting, and with one slot it receives the first two runs. This violates the documented per-agent fair share; overdue tickets should still be counted against the agent's share even though they are not deferred.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitequeue.py:order (overdue branch)
